﻿# IAS 12 â€” Income Taxes

IAS 12 covers current tax and deferred tax arising from temporary differences, unused tax losses, and tax credits.

## Key ideas

The core study distinction is between the current tax calculation and the deferred tax consequences of differences between accounting carrying amounts and tax bases. Recognition depends on the relevant recovery and probability conditions.

## Connections

IAS 12 connects to [[IFRS_1_First_Time_Adoption]], [[IAS_16_Property_Plant_Equipment]], and [[IAS_36_Impairment]].

nodes.name: IAS_16_Property_Plant_Equipment
nodes.summary: ﻿# IAS 16 â€” Property, Plant and Equipment

knowledgeMeta.content:
﻿# IAS 16 â€” Property, Plant and Equipment

IAS 16 addresses recognition, initial measurement, depreciation, subsequent measurement, and derecognition of tangible operating assets.

## Key ideas

Study follows the recognition criteria, component accounting, useful lives and residual values, cost and revaluation models, impairment indicators, and disposal accounting.

## Connections

IAS 16 connects to [[IAS_36_Impairment]], [[IFRS_1_First_Time_Adoption]], and [[IAS_12_Income_Taxes]].

nodes.name: IAS_28_Investments_Associates
nodes.summary: ﻿# IAS 28 â€” Investments in Associates and Joint Ventures

knowledgeMeta.content:
﻿# IAS 28 â€” Investments in Associates and Joint Ventures

IAS 28 addresses the equity method for investments in associates and joint ventures.

﻿# IAS 2 â€” Inventories

IAS 2 addresses the measurement and expense recognition of inventories.

## Key ideas

Inventories are measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value. Cost formulas, write-downs, reversals, and the point at which inventory becomes an expense are central study themes.

## Connections

IAS 2 connects to [[IFRS_15_Revenue]], [[IAS_36_Impairment]], and [[IFRS_Study_Method]].

﻿# IAS 32 â€” Financial Instruments Presentation

IAS 32 addresses presentation, classification, and offsetting of financial instruments.

﻿# IAS 36 â€” Impairment of Assets

IAS 36 sets out when assets and cash-generating units are tested for impairment and how recoverable amount is determined.

## Key ideas

The main concepts are impairment indicators, value in use, fair value less costs of disposal, cash-generating units, allocation of impairment losses, and reversal restrictions.

## Connections

IAS 36 connects to [[IAS_16_Property_Plant_Equipment]], [[IFRS_16_Leases]], and [[IFRS_1_First_Time_Adoption]].

﻿# IAS 37 â€” Provisions and Contingencies

IAS 37 distinguishes provisions from contingent liabilities and contingent assets and sets recognition and measurement principles.

## Key ideas

A provision requires a present obligation from a past event, a probable outflow, and a reliable estimate. The standard also guides disclosure where recognition criteria are not met.

## Connections

IAS 37 connects to [[IFRS_1_First_Time_Adoption]], [[IAS_12_Income_Taxes]], and [[IFRS_15_Revenue]].

﻿# IFRS 10 â€” Consolidated Financial Statements

IFRS 10 uses control as the basis for determining when an investor consolidates an investee.

## Key ideas

The control assessment considers power over the investee, exposure or rights to variable returns, and the ability to use power to affect those returns. Consolidation then requires combining the relevant financial information and eliminating intragroup effects.

## Connections

IFRS 10 connects to [[IAS_28_Investments_Associates]], [[IFRS_3_Business_Combinations]], and [[IFRS_12_Interests_Other_Entities]].

nodes.name: IFRS_15_Revenue
nodes.summary: ﻿# IFRS 15 â€” Revenue from Contracts with Customers

knowledgeMeta.content:
﻿# IFRS 15 â€” Revenue from Contracts with Customers

IFRS 15 provides a principles-based model for recognising revenue from contracts with customers.

## Five-step model

The study sequence is to identify the contract, identify performance obligations, determine the transaction price, allocate that price, and recognise revenue when or as performance obligations are satisfied.

## Connections

IFRS 15 connects to [[IFRS_Study_Method]], [[IFRS_16_Leases]], and [[IFRS_1_First_Time_Adoption]].

﻿# IFRS 16 â€” Leases

IFRS 16 establishes a lessee model that generally recognises a right-of-use asset and lease liability, subject to specified exemptions.

## Key ideas

A useful study route is to identify whether an arrangement contains a lease, measure the initial liability and right-of-use asset, understand subsequent depreciation and interest, and distinguish lease modifications and exemptions.

## Connections

IFRS 16 connects to [[IFRS_Study_Method]], [[IAS_36_Impairment]], and [[IFRS_1_First_Time_Adoption]].

﻿# IFRS 1 â€” First-time Adoption

IFRS 1 establishes the framework for an entity preparing its first financial statements that explicitly and unreservedly comply with IFRS Accounting Standards.

## Key ideas

The adoption process centres on a date of transition, an opening IFRS statement of financial position, consistent accounting policies, and transparent reconciliations from previous GAAP. IFRS 1 combines a general retrospective principle with specific optional exemptions and mandatory exceptions.

## Connections

IFRS 1 connects to [[IFRS_Study_Method]], [[IAS_16_Property_Plant_Equipment]], [[IAS_36_Impairment]], and [[IFRS_9_Financial_Instruments]].

﻿# IFRS 3 â€” Business Combinations

IFRS 3 addresses acquisition accounting, goodwill, and identifiable assets and liabilities in a business combination.

﻿# IFRS 7 â€” Financial Instruments Disclosures

IFRS 7 requires disclosures that help users evaluate the significance of financial instruments and the risks arising from them.

﻿# IFRS 9 â€” Financial Instruments

IFRS 9 addresses classification and measurement of financial assets and liabilities, impairment, and hedge accounting.

## Key ideas

Study commonly follows the business-model and contractual-cash-flow assessment, expected credit loss model, and the relationship between risk management and hedge accounting. The standard links closely with presentation and disclosure requirements in IAS 32 and IFRS 7.

## Connections

IFRS 9 connects to [[IAS_32_Financial_Instruments_Presentation]], [[IFRS_7_Financial_Instruments_Disclosures]], and [[IFRS_Study_Method]].

﻿# IFRS Study Method

This collection is organised as a connected study map rather than a replacement for the authoritative standards.

## Suggested route

Start with the purpose and recognition model of each standard, then map measurement, presentation, disclosure, and common judgement areas. Use the original source PDFs in the IFRS Study folder for detailed requirements and exam preparation.

## Connections

The study method connects every topic in this collection, including [[IFRS_1_First_Time_Adoption]], [[IFRS_9_Financial_Instruments]], [[IFRS_15_Revenue]], [[IFRS_16_Leases]], [[IFRS_10_Consolidation]], [[IAS_2_Inventories]], [[IAS_12_Income_Taxes]], [[IAS_16_Property_Plant_Equipment]], [[IAS_36_Impairment]], and [[IAS_37_Provisions]].
